title: Architecture Constraint
description: The frontmatter of constraints/<constraint-slug>.md. No subtypes. A constraint limits the solution space: integration strategies, storage, timing, how the processes behave while they run, quality demands — «they constrain the solution, never the domain» (SPEC-003 §Architecture Constraint). It is the last of the homes a fact is tried against — «A fact takes the first of these homes that holds it» (SPEC-003 §Rule): what an operation answers is the contract's `answers`, a condition on an element or on an operation is a Rule, and «The stack is never a node» (SPEC-003 §Rule) — a language, a runtime version, a package, a tool, a command, an image, a test arrangement is the project's standard. What it cannot be is a domain rule wearing an architecture name — that is a Rule. Nor is it a project's own arrangement convention wearing a system-wide name: a constraint holds what the solution must have regardless of which project or stack encodes it, and how one project's source achieves that — even the identical property — is a standard's rule, never a second entry here. The body carries `## Description`.

case.description: One sentence naming what this node does not decide, naming no node.

node.description: The node that decides the case, as a reference: a bare slug inside this node's directory, the full identity everywhere else.

excludes.description: The boundaries another node decides — «Any node may declare `excludes`: a list of entries, each a `case` — one sentence naming what this node does not decide — and the `node` that decides it, written as a reference (R2)» (SPEC-003 §The five classes). «It adds no obligation» (SPEC-003 §The five classes): a boundary declared here is one the validator resolves, and is not written into the prose a second time.

statement.description: One falsifiable condition over the implementation. Stated in one sentence: the sentence count is the half of this the validator decides, and a second sentence is refused — it is a second rule, a scenario, or an element's definition, each with a home of its own.

scope.description: `system`, or the context slug the constraint is confined to.

fitness.description: The mechanical check that verifies the constraint, where one exists — stated as the condition it decides, never as a command or a step. Which step of a project runs it is that project's registry's to declare, in `commands[].decides` of `schemas/standard.json`: the node stays what the solution must have, and the registry stays how one project checks it.

examples.statement: Events between contexts travel asynchronously; no context calls another synchronously to publish a fact.
